title: prefill+decode: chunked speculative prefill + kernel scheduler + KV cache & continuous batching optimizations
author: Evan Liu
description: Motivation: reduce tail latency and improve throughput for mixed prefill+decode workloads by overlapping prefill and decode stages, chunking long prefill sequences, and using speculative prefill when small prefix changes are detected. This PR combines four coordinated changes: 1) chunked prefill path that breaks long prefill requests into fixed-size chunks to reduce NV memory pressure and improve kernel reuse; 2) speculative prefill where the runtime issues lightweight speculative KV merges for common prefix continuations to avoid a full prefill round-trip when decode extends a recent prefix; 3) a kernel selection scheduler that prioritizes low-latency kernel variants for in-flight decode slices while batching long-running prefill chunks; 4) KV cache lifecycle and continuous batching fixes to correctly merge speculative entries and avoid double-counting tokens in billing/metrics. Summary of impact: end-to-end 95th percentile latency reduced by ~12-18% on 8k context LLaMA-style models; steady-state throughput improved by 15-25% depending on request mix (higher gains for workloads with many long prefill requests followed by short decodes). Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (ENG-1147) - [x] microbenchmarks added - [x] integration tests for KV merge and rollback - [x] perf canary run passed against perf-lab - [x] docs updated with config knobs Implementation notes: implemented chunked prefill in runtime/prefill_manager.cc with chunk size configurable via PREFILL_CHUNK_SIZE; speculative prefill is opt-in via runtime flags and guarded by a per-route policy that checks prefix age and token delta; kernel scheduler (runtime/kernel_scheduler.{cc,h}) introduces a lightweight prioritizer based on request urgency and expected kernel latency; KV cache changes (runtime/kv_cache.cc) add a transient speculative layer and explicit commit/rollback semantics; continuous batching fixes handle deadline propagation for speculative prefill flows. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged unless the speculative prefill or chunked prefill flags are enabled. Rollout plan: feature gated by default, will enable on Dedicated canaries, then staged rollout to hosted tier with metrics gating. Related: follows on previous prefill/decode overlap work (see PRs ~#40k-46k).
commits: 3 commits: 1) add chunked prefill and config knobs; 2) kernel scheduler + prioritizer; 3) KV cache speculative layer and tests; commit messages are concise and tests are split across commits for reviewability
review_comments: Aisha Patel: Can you explain how speculative prefill avoids token double-counting in metrics? Please add a unit test covering commit/rollback edge cases.

Evan Liu: Added explicit commit/rollback and unit tests in tests/unit/kv_cache_speculative_test.cc; metrics now attribute speculative tokens to a transient bucket and only commit to main counters on successful commit.

Diego Ramos: Kernel scheduler looks good but please add a small integration test ensuring decode slices are prioritized under high contention; also ensure scheduler config defaults are safe for small GPU memory instances.
Evan Liu: Added integration test in tests/perf/prefill_decode_bench.cc and tuned defaults to conservative values; documented knobs in docs/perf/prefill-decode-optimizations.md.
Claire Morgan: CI flaky on first run due to perf-suite timeout; re-run passed. Approved.
release_notes: Runtime: prefilling and decode throughput/latency improvements via chunked prefill, speculative prefill, kernel scheduler prioritization, and KV cache commit semantics. Feature gated; opt-in via PREFILL_CHUNKED=true and SPECULATIVE_PREFILL=true. Expected 12-25% throughput/latency improvements for mixed workloads.
